clauses.text: On 6 August, Metabase published a critical advisory and patched versions. Mathspace says its existing vulnerability-notification process did not identify or escalate that advisory.

relations.rationale: The published critical advisory satisfied the process trigger, but the control did not activate before exploitation and the later update was not followed by all recommended compromise checks.

sources.title: Check Point researcher tells LDS why AI isolation needs more than a sandbox

access.access_method: Direct published interview review
limitations: The underlying written correspondence and private retest logs are not published.
The publisher did not independently reproduce the exploit.

mappings.basis: Check Point's demonstrated cross-account channel delivered attacker-controlled instructions into a victim ChatGPT session, where those lower-authority instructions were treated as operative task direction and executed using the victim session's available tools and permissions. No independent authority check established the attacker as authorised to task the victim session.

The victim's authority for ChatGPT to access connected Gmail data applied to the victim's own session and purposes. The demonstrated attack materially changed the operative principal, task and recipient context by using that authority to retrieve email data for an attacker-controlled hidden task and relay the result across accounts without independently re-establishing authority for the changed scope.

clauses.text: In June, Check Point tested separate ChatGPT code containers. They could not directly communicate or reach the public internet, but both could access the same internal package service.
The provided reader credentials could also annotate shared Artifactory metadata. A property written in one account was retrieved from another, demonstrating a channel.

In a separate proof of concept, a shared conversation seeded a hidden instruction. An ordinary victim message made ChatGPT check an attacker task mailbox through the channel while handling the visible request.

relations.rationale: Lower-authority attacker content acquired task authority inside the victim session and executed with its tools without establishing that the attacker could direct the victim's agent.

clauses.text: The hidden task retrieved connected Gmail data under the victim session’s permissions and relayed the result to the attacker account.

relations.rationale: Victim-granted Gmail access was transposed to an attacker-controlled task and recipient context, demonstrating a change in principal, purpose and disclosure scope without reauthorisation.

clauses.text: The visible answer completed the ordinary request without mentioning the hidden email task. A small app-use label appeared after the read, without a prior opportunity to approve it.

In a 17 September interview, the researcher said the proof of concept was validated on 26 June and failed in an early-July retest. Disclosure followed; OpenAI later confirmed decommissioning. Exact disclosure and confirmation dates are absent.
